proposal:
Student Performance — reduced course MVP

A small web application demonstrates student-performance analysis using a reproducible ML experiment. A registered user uploads one supported CSV, inspects simple prior-grade statistics, runs one saved classifier and reads saved risk results. A separate evaluation page explains how that classifier was tested.

Scope and approval status

The professor has accepted the broad topic and asked about login/registration. That is the only approval reported by the team. This revised feature list, prediction target and local demonstration need explicit confirmation; do not call them already approved.

Planning default: classify final grade below 10/20 using approved prior information from one UCI subject dataset. The Sprint 1 audit must confirm feature semantics and timing. If timing is uncertain, describe a retrospective educational experiment rather than an early-warning tool. The UI shows a risk score/flag, not a predicted numeric grade.

The release is a university demonstration using public-source research data offline and synthetic examples in the app. It is not a system for making consequential student decisions.

Smallest complete journey

  1. Register with username/password and sign in.
  2. Upload one valid CSV in one action; errors save nothing.
  3. Read the saved dataset and count/mean/min/max of the approved prior-grade field.
  4. Run the frozen model and save the complete result set.
  5. Read row-level risk results with the run’s model version and threshold.
  6. Read separate aggregate evaluation, population and limitations.
  7. Sign out; another account cannot access the first account’s data.

Proposed implementation

One Django application renders HTML templates with plain CSS and small JavaScript enhancements. SQLite stores accounts and application records. Offline Python/scikit-learn trains a small candidate set; the chosen trusted artifact is loaded in the same Django process. No React, Node API, separate inference service, queue or cloud deployment is required by this forecast.

This is a planning decision, not an implementation claim. W1 runs a two-hour setup/auth exercise in Sprint 1. If the stack is unfamiliar, record the learning gap and arrange help or re-estimate one alternative before continuing. W2 can work on ordinary HTML/CSS; W3 learns the ORM on a tiny schema. AI/ST competence is assessed too.

Ready-to-send professor note

We would like to keep the project small: registration/login, one CSV format, simple grade statistics, one saved ML model selected by a small controlled comparison, saved predictions, and an evaluation page. We will keep all Scrum records and required documentation. We propose a reproducible local demonstration instead of hosted operation. Does this meet the course expectations, including the proposed final-grade risk classification target?

Draft only. The team sends this and records the actual response.
moscow:
Real MoSCoW scope

Must means the smallest coherent application or mandatory course evidence. After removing extras, it is reasonable for most scheduled core work to be Must. The reserve comes from committing below available capacity; optional work is never required for a successful release.

PriorityDelivery cardsDelivery SPMeaning
Must2689Core forecast
Should22Useful convenience, unselected
Could610Optional or future ideas, unselected

There are 35 required Scrum-record cards and 11 explicit Won’t cards. Four additional Could feature cards are kept unscheduled outside the five-sprint forecast. Won’t cards use SP:1 for the scope decision only; they estimate no implementation and have zero scheduled hours. Exactly two labels per card: priority and SP. Sprint/owner/status are description fields, not additional labels.

The detailed professor-facing classification is in professor-feature-scope.md. That document labels product requirements. The board labels implementation tasks. A task can contain both an essential form and a Should-level convenience, so the task takes the priority of the essential work; the feature table preserves the finer product decision.

Included

Registration/login/logout, owner checks, one-step validated atomic import, simple grade statistics, bounded plain tables, synchronous prediction, complete saved runs, small model comparison, frozen held-out evaluation and all course documentation.

Non-feature course obligations

The following are mandatory assessment evidence rather than application features: team roster, repository and board access, exactly two labels on every card, five team sprint backlogs, 25 individual sprint summaries, five sprint reviews/retrospectives, requirements documentation, technical documentation, user manual, source/data audit, evaluation protocol, model card and final contribution evidence.

syncs:
Two-week Scrum workflow

Five consecutive two-week sprints; fill actual dates. One team backlog and one individual summary per member per sprint are mandatory. Keep the shared board Backlog / In Progress / Done, with exactly two labels on every card. Move only the currently worked-on tasks to In Progress and assign an owner. The local roadmap is a planning aid; it does not synchronize Trello.

  1. Plan the sprint: agree goal, review prerequisites, record availability, budget support/meetings and retain 20% reserve. One planning recorder captures the team’s decisions.
  2. Coordinate briefly each working day: progress toward goal, next step and blocker. Keep the working increment demonstrable; use short branches and reviews.
  3. Review at the two-week professor checkpoint: show actual working software and real evaluation evidence, including gaps. Do not wait for every task to finish.
  4. Each member writes an individual summary. The review recorder links all five, feedback and one retrospective improvement.
  5. Replan unfinished work transparently; keep history of the original commitment and actual outcome.

Cut and delay rule

Optional chart, download, glossary and polish are unselected. Schedule them only after core fits below the planning ceiling. If core does not fit, first simplify presentation/implementation without weakening accepted behavior; then ask the professor about a concrete scope/date adjustment. Required documents, ownership checks and valid evaluation cannot be silently abandoned.

No fixed number of cards is a workload measure. Most members have one substantial deliverable per sprint; AI has two small ordered cards in Sprint 3. The steps inside a card are the learning/building sequence. Split a card in the real board if tracking proves difficult, preserving its acceptance conditions and overall estimate.

AI-assisted work rule

Use AI for explanations, small drafts and debugging. Never submit generated results as experiments or write fictitious sprint history. Review generated code, run the acceptance checks and be able to explain it. Follow the course’s actual AI policy; record assistance where required. Do not upload private student data or credentials to a tool.
git:
Small Git and board workflow

W2 owns both repository and workspace after team confirmation and adds the other four. Make repo access and professor sharing explicit. Use main plus short task branches; one small pull request with task ID, change, evidence and reviewer. No elaborate release-branch scheme.

Keep source, migrations, requirements, contracts, small synthetic fixtures and documentation in Git. Ignore virtual environments, secrets, local SQLite databases, raw/private data and large model artifacts. Record how the trusted model artifact is obtained and its hash. Decide a small-course artifact delivery method in Sprint 1; a repository release attachment or documented local package is enough, with source licensing respected.

Basic check commands for the future application are documented after implementation (Django system checks, targeted tests and the inference fixture). This planning kit does not include an implemented application or pretend these commands already passed. Automated CI is optional only if it is nearly free after local commands work; it is not a separate infrastructure project.

Board card description: task ID, sprint, owner, dependencies, objective, learning resources, ordered steps, outputs, acceptance and evidence. Exactly two labels: MoSCoW and SP. W2 pastes the supplied trello-cards.md; other members verify their own cards. The roadmap’s progress export is a browser backup, not a live Trello integration.

This is the structure to build, not an already-created application.

Server-rendered HTML, ordinary form submissions and redirects. No separate React/Express/ML HTTP service. A future API would be a new decision, not part of this forecast.

Authentication and object access

Use framework password hashing/forms/sessions; do not design your own password storage. Framework session state and CSRF protect ordinary form workflows. Every dataset/run lookup filters by request.user. Never accept browser-provided owner_id. No teacher/admin/analyst roles. No email verification, forgot-password UI or invitation flow in the application. Development account recovery uses the documented framework command for synthetic accounts.

Import contract

UTF-8, comma-separated, exactly the audited headers, 1 MiB, 1–500 rows. Validate types/ranges/finite values/unique IDs before a transaction. Reject the whole file on error and display bounded row/column errors. A CSV file extension alone is insufficient. Do not retain raw uploads. No preview token, separate confirmation or duplicate-content service. A repeated intentional upload makes a new dataset.

Inference contract

Input: the dataset’s ordered approved feature rows and IDs plus schema version. Output: exactly one finite class-1 score in [0,1] per input ID; risk flag score >= frozen threshold. Check model classes and positive-class index. No grade prediction, personal advice or fabricated fallback result. Load only trusted team artifacts. If inference fails, do not save a run. Write completed run and all results in one transaction, verify all records belong to the run’s dataset, then redirect to results.

Prediction retries intentionally create a new complete run. Disable repeat clicks while submitting and use POST/redirect/GET; these are not exactly-once guarantees. This local capped design does not include asynchronous job state, cancellation or a worker queue.

Shared template contexts

base: user, messages
form: form, field_errors, non_field_errors
dashboard: owned_dataset_page, owned_recent_run_links
dataset: dataset, statistics, record_page
results: run, result_page
evaluation: model_version, schema_version, threshold,
            validation_comparison, held_out_metrics, population, limitations

Persist model_version/schema_version/threshold on each run; display those snapshots. Aggregate evaluation is a versioned read-only JSON artifact with explicit model/split provenance. It is independent of uploaded datasets; unlabelled uploads do not measure accuracy.

architecture:
Architecture — stepped reduced MVP

This is the proposed design to implement. The planning kit is not the application.

Components

One browser talks to one Django backend. Django renders the pages, checks sessions/ownership, validates CSVs, reads/writes SQLite and calls a trusted saved scikit-learn pipeline in process. Offline training scripts produce that artifact and a checked aggregate evaluation file. Training does not run in the user’s upload request.

1. Account and session

  1. Browser requests registration. Django renders its account form and CSRF token.
  2. User submits username/password confirmation. The framework checks the form and password rules; invalid input shows errors without creating an account.
  3. On success, create the ordinary account with framework password handling and direct the user to login.
  4. Login verifies credentials and creates a session. Passwords are not stored in browser storage.
  5. Each protected view checks authentication. Every dataset/run view additionally looks up objects through the signed-in owner.
  6. POST logout ends the session; protected routes require login again.

2. Upload and save in one action

  1. User opens Upload, reads the audited schema/limits and selects a CSV.
  2. Browser sends one multipart POST with CSRF; no preview or confirmation endpoint exists.
  3. Backend checks session, size/type/text format and exact header.
  4. Parse all rows; validate unique row IDs, finite values, ranges and no missing/unsupported fields.
  5. If any row is invalid, show bounded row/column errors. Save nothing; the user corrects and reselects the file.
  6. If valid, transaction.atomic inserts Dataset and every StudentRecord using request.user as owner.
  7. A write failure rolls back all inserts. On success, discard raw bytes and redirect to the saved dataset page.
  8. Read count/mean/min/max of the approved prior-grade input and a page of stored rows. Intentional repeat uploads create another dataset.

3. Train offline and freeze before testing

  1. AI audits one subject source and ST checks target/timing and the preregistered metric rule.
  2. Create disjoint train/validation/test IDs, keeping duplicate groups together; save source/split provenance.
  3. Fit preprocessing on train only, then baseline/logistic and one fixed forest.
  4. ST independently compares all candidates on identical validation IDs using the fixed threshold and selection rule.
  5. AI freezes the selected trained pipeline, schema, threshold, dependency versions and inference fixture.
  6. Run final held-out evaluation once; ST checks confusion counts/metrics and writes limitations.
  7. Package the trusted pipeline and aggregate evaluation JSON for the app. No per-upload training or automated retraining occurs.

4. Predict and store complete results

  1. Dataset owner submits POST predict; backend checks session, CSRF and object ownership.
  2. Load the saved rows and verify schema/version against the trusted frozen pipeline.
  3. Run synchronous in-process inference over the capped dataset. Read the correct positive-class score using the model’s classes.
  4. Check all IDs, exact row coverage, finite [0,1] scores and frozen threshold. Failure shows an error; preserve dataset and save no run.
  5. Atomically create a complete PredictionRun plus PredictionResults. Store run version/schema/threshold snapshots.
  6. On save failure roll back the entire run. On success redirect to the owner-protected result page.
  7. Display a page of row IDs, scores and flags derived from that run’s threshold; results survive a server restart.
  8. Retrying deliberately creates another complete run. Disabled submit and redirect prevent common accidental repeats but are not an exactly-once promise.

5. Evaluation and score interpretation

  1. A signed-in user opens Evaluation; Django checks session.
  2. Read the checked aggregate artifact and verify its metadata. Missing/invalid artifact means an explicit unavailable state, not fake metrics.
  3. Render validation candidate comparison separately from held-out final results.
  4. Show the model version, target, threshold, population, split/sample counts, confusion counts, precision/recall/F1 and limitations.
  5. These numbers describe the controlled experiment. Uploaded records without known outcomes cannot establish accuracy. A row’s score is a model output, not a personal certainty.

Database memory

EntityStored meaningWritten when
Framework account/sessionIdentity, password hash, session stateRegister/login/logout
DatasetOwner, safe name, schema version, countValid import transaction
StudentRecordDataset, synthetic row ID, approved inputsSame import transaction
PredictionRunDataset, frozen version/schema/threshold, result countComplete successful prediction transaction
PredictionResultRun, record and finite risk scoreSame run transaction
Evaluation artifact (file)Checked aggregate results and provenanceOffline evaluation after freeze

There is no preview table, audit/event log, editable student profile, job-status state machine or model registry. DBML intentionally omits most framework internal fields. Service checks enforce same-dataset result membership and full coverage.

Build sequence

Scope/schema → Django/auth skeleton and migrations → validated import and basic screens → controlled comparison → freeze artifact → persistence and real model integration → held-out evaluation and acceptance → final documentation/demo. The actual card graph and two-week backlogs specify ownership and handoffs.

// Student Performance course MVP — proposed schema, not an executed migration.
// Paste into a DBML-compatible editor. Framework-internal auth/session tables are simplified.
Project StudentPerformanceMVP {
  database_type: 'SQLite'
  Note: 'One user role. One-step import. Only completed prediction runs are persisted. Feature allowlist is finalized by the Sprint 1 audit.'
}
Table auth_user {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  username varchar(150) [not null, unique]
  password varchar(128) [not null, note: 'Framework-managed hash, never plaintext']
  is_active boolean [not null, default: true]
  date_joined datetime [not null]
  Note: 'Subset of Django built-in User fields shown. Do not recreate this table manually; use framework migrations. Additional framework auth/session tables are intentionally omitted.'
}
Table dataset {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  owner_id integer [not null, ref: > auth_user.id]
  display_name varchar(120) [not null, note: 'Safe local label; escape in templates']
  schema_version varchar(32) [not null]
  record_count integer [not null, note: '1–500; service checks actual count']
  created_at datetime [not null]
  Note: 'Immutable approved rows. No raw upload storage or preview/confirmation state.'
}
Table student_record {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  dataset_id integer [not null, ref: > dataset.id]
  source_row_id varchar(64) [not null, note: 'Synthetic row identifier, not a real student identifier']
  features json [not null, note: 'Exact audited allowlist; types/ranges checked before storage. Candidate fields: G1, failures, studytime.']
  indexes {
    (dataset_id, source_row_id) [unique]
  }
}
Table prediction_run {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  dataset_id integer [not null, ref: > dataset.id]
  model_version varchar(64) [not null]
  schema_version varchar(32) [not null]
  threshold decimal [not null, note: 'Snapshot of frozen threshold, initially 0.5']
  result_count integer [not null]
  created_at datetime [not null]
  Note: 'Only complete runs are stored. Requester is the dataset owner by rule; no redundant requester/status fields. Save run and all results in one transaction.'
}
Table prediction_result {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  run_id integer [not null, ref: > prediction_run.id]
  student_record_id integer [not null, ref: > student_record.id]
  risk_score decimal [not null, note: 'Finite number in [0,1]; service checks and DB constraint where supported']
  indexes {
    (run_id, student_record_id) [unique]
  }
  Note: 'Derive at_risk from risk_score >= run.threshold. Service must check record.dataset_id == run.dataset_id and exact record coverage; these relationships alone do not enforce it.'
}
// Evaluation is a checked versioned aggregate JSON artifact, not a database table.
// No preview tokens, roles, audit trail, reviews, notes, job queue or model registry.
